title: Neki van – Expressing “To Have” in Hungarian

sections.heading: How Hungarian expresses “to have”
paragraphs: In Hungarian, the concept of “to have” is expressed using the structure “neki van.”
This does not follow regular verb patterns and must be learned separately.

sections.heading: Neki van = to have
paragraphs: Hungarian does not have a direct verb meaning “to have.”
Instead, it uses a structure that means something like “To him/her there is...” combined with the verb “van” and a possessive ending.

sections.heading: Possession with van
paragraphs: Here are the main patterns of possession in affirmative, negative, and question forms.

rows: Nekem van autóm. (I have a car.)
Nekem nincs autóm. (I don’t have a car.)
Van autód? (Do you have a car?)
Neked van könyved. (You have a book.)
Neked nincs könyved. (You don’t have a book.)
Van könyve? (Does he/she have a book?)
Neki van macskája. (He/She has a cat.)
Neki nincs macskája. (He/She doesn’t have a cat.)
Van macskájuk? (Do they have a cat?)
Nekünk van házunk. (We have a house.)
Nekünk nincs házunk. (We don’t have a house.)
Van házunk? (Do we have a house?)
Nektek van tollatok. (You all have a pen.)
Nektek nincs tollatok. (You all don’t have a pen.)
Van tollatok? (Do you all have a pen?)
Nekik van kertjük. (They have a garden.)
Nekik nincs kertjük. (They don’t have a garden.)
Van kertjük? (Do they have a garden?)

sections.heading: Examples
list: Neked van testvéred? (Do you have a sibling?)
Nekik nincs autójuk. (They don’t have a car.)
